claims.text: A Si-20Cr-20Fe silicide coating can improve the high-temperature oxidation resistance of MoNbTaTiW RHEA.
The coating protects by transforming into an adherent, dense oxide during high-temperature exposure.
The untreated MoNbTaTiW alloy, or a similar RHEA, has insufficient high-temperature oxidation resistance.
A Si-20Cr-20Fe coating can be deposited on MoNbTaTiW RHEA by a fused slurry method.
A controlled post-deposition oxidation heat treatment is a necessary part of the proposed coating intervention.
The coating should remain effective during exposure at 1100°C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere for 200 hours.
Exposure at 1100°C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere for 200 hours mimics extreme structural-service environments.
The as-deposited coating has an outer high-silicon layer mainly composed of MSi2 and an inner lower-silicon layer mainly containing M5Si3.
After high-temperature oxidation, the coating consists of an outer oxide layer and an inner silicide layer.
The silicide coating acts as a reservoir of silicon and reactive Cr and Fe.
During high-temperature oxidation, silicon diffuses from the coating toward the RHEA substrate.
Oxidation of silicon forms a continuous, slow-growing oxide barrier.
The coating-derived oxide barrier lowers oxygen diffusivity and thereby limits subsequent oxidation.
The coated alloy will show significantly lower oxidation weight gain than the untreated alloy under the same conditions.
The coated alloy will form a stable, adherent oxide scale relative to the untreated alloy.
A prior RHEA oxidation study reported a weight gain of approximately 4.03 mg/cm² after 200 hours at 1100°C.
The intervention will be effective only if the coating is deposited uniformly.
The magnitude of the reduction in oxidation weight gain is uncertain without experimental validation.
The long-term adherence and stability of the oxide under thermal cycling and mechanical stress remain unverified.
Failure to achieve at least a 50% reduction in oxidation weight gain, or formation of a discontinuous and nonprotective scale, would falsify the hypothesis.
